mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which positively impacts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rate indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rises above 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: Combined growth in employment and low unemployment suggests a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Both employment and unemployment metrics are favorable but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth during late-cycle expansion signals continued economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in late-cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate stimulates economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPI > 200) leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days due to potential rate hikes.
failure_condition: CPI exceeds 200 but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate combined with low retail sales indicates economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: High FEDFUNDS and low RSAFS but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts in early-cycle recovery boost economic confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in early-cycle.
